dropIns.name: Mill Square
dropIns.description: The square where every road in the vale starts, on market day.

dropIns.name: Moor Top
dropIns.description: A knoll above the drove road, with the whole moor ahead of it.

dropIns.name: The Quarry
dropIns.description: The quarry bench under the crag, beside the cliff the Greystone Caves open in.

dropIns.name: Stepping Stones
dropIns.description: By the heron hide at the foot of The Crossing, over the stepping stones from the west bank.

dropIns.name: The Strand
dropIns.description: The strand where the road comes down to the sea.

dropIns.name: Farmhouse
dropIns.description: The yard of the farm at Orchard Terraces, at the top of the terraces.

dropIns.name: The Dam
dropIns.description: The forecourt of the power station, under the dam, with the switchyard gone to grass beyond it.

dropIns.name: Rest House
dropIns.description: The rest house in the middle of the reserve, the dry ground a raid stops at.

dropIns.name: Salvage Camp
dropIns.description: The salvage camp on the beach under the east cape, with the wreck out on the reef.

dropIns.name: Old Quay
dropIns.description: The quay of the drowned port, where the jetty from the strand comes in.

dropIns.name: Cove Steps
dropIns.description: The cliff top over the cove, where the steps go down.

people.name: Trader
lines: Fresh from the orchards over the river. Well. Over the road.
The road east takes you on to The Crossing.

people.name: Ada
lines: There is a cave up in the peaks. Mum says it goes all the way to the sea.

people.name: Pip
lines: Race you to the fountain!
I always win. Ada says that does not count because I start closer.

people.name: Old Peg
lines: Everything on that stall was cheaper before you got here.
Everything was cheaper before anybody got here.

people.name: Stallholder
lines: Apples from the orchard, down the lane past the brook.
Or pick them yourself. Everybody else does.

people.name: Miller
lines: The pond turns the wheel all year. It would be nice if it paid as well.
The brook runs right through the village and comes out at Tom’s pool.

people.name: Old Wick
lines: Nothing in this pond but Magikarp and regret.
Mind, if you have a rod, press at the water. It costs you nothing but time.

people.name: Carter
lines: I lost my purse somewhere round this yard. Do not tell the board.
It told everyone.

people.name: Grandpa Ott
lines: This is the oldest cottage in the vale.
When I was a boy there was snow on the peaks all summer.

people.name: Digger
lines: Dig, plant, chase off the Oddish. Dig, plant, chase off the Oddish.
It is a living. It is not a good one.

people.name: Mrs Marlow
lines: I grow beans. Ott says he grows beans. Those are not beans.

people.name: Fern
lines: There is a garden behind the woodcutter’s, walled off by one small tree.
Old Hazel left it. Nobody with a Cut has been past in years.

people.name: Nan Birch
lines: Sit down, you look terrible.
Everybody who comes through here looks terrible. It is the raids.

people.name: Bram
lines: My mum says never to go down to the pool on your own.
Tom goes down there on his own. Tom is ten.

people.name: Gardener
lines: Every Pidgey in the vale nests in my roof.
East of the village the road goes over the bridge at The Crossing.

people.name: Mrs Lark
lines: Best in show, nine years running. There is no show. I started it. I judge it.

people.name: Lost Walker
lines: Is this the way to the marsh? I have been going round this tree for some time.
South, you say. Down the lane. Yes. Obviously.

people.name: Drover
lines: That Tauros has walked off this moor and back four times this year.
Up the road, mind the ledges. They only go down.

people.name: Gatekeeper
lines: I keep the gate. There is no gate. It is a very quiet job.
East: The Crossing, and the only bridge for miles.
calls: Mind the gate. There is none.

people.name: Wayfarer
lines: The Westward Road goes out of the vale, if you need to go out in a hurry.
Most people who come through do.

people.name: Picker
lines: The berries grow back by the next raid. Do not ask me how. I just pick.

people.name: Woodcutter
lines: A proper axe would clear that little tree by the garden in one go.
I have a blunt one and a bad back. You want a Pokemon that knows Cut.

people.name: Tom
lines: The pool is full of Magikarp!
Nobody believes me. There is something on the island too. Mind the gaps.

people.name: Miller’s Boy
lines: Mind the sacks. I have counted them. I am going to count them again.
The wheel has not stopped in eighty years. Nobody knows how to stop it.

people.name: Nurse
lines: The machines are spoken for, I am afraid. There is a raid on, you know.
If you are hurt, the pump on the green has medicine by it. Nobody counts it.

people.name: Clerk
lines: Sorry, nothing on the shelves till the boat comes in.
Professor Oak’s parcel? We sent it out by the lane. It will be lying about somewhere.

people.name: Mrs Ott
lines: He told you about the snow, did he.
There was no snow.

people.name: Drover Boy
lines: Grandad says they know the way home.
They do. They go there. All the time. Without me.

people.name: Lina
lines: I count them every time and get a different number.
I got six once. There were never six.

people.name: Tarn Fisher
lines: Up on the moor the water has nothing in it but sky.
I come for the quiet. Well. I did.

people.name: Peak Walker
lines: East is the quarry, and the caves under it. Mind who you meet in there.
I have been meaning to go. I have been meaning to go for years.

people.name: Walker
lines: Going up? You will not get down the way you came, not by the ledges. They only go one way.
Quick, mind. Very quick.

people.name: Shepherd
lines: The tarn never freezes, whatever the winter.
There was a sheep track west, under it, to the old chapel.
By day the fog turns you back. Go after dark, if you go.

people.name: Shepherd’s Lad
lines: Grandad says they are sheep. They have horns and they are poisonous.
I asked when we might get a sheep. He went very quiet.

people.name: Toll Clerk
lines: Nobody has paid the toll in forty years, but I still have to write it down.
That is nobody, again. You are the fourth nobody today.

people.name: Mother Stone
lines: They sing at night, the stones. Clefairy come up to hear it.
I have counted them twice tonight. Nine and eleven. It is a good sign, or the other thing.

people.name: Drover’s Wife
lines: You touch the Grey Stones for luck, going up and coming down.
He touched them every time for thirty years. Then a Tauros sat on him. So.

people.name: Camp Cook
lines: It is stew. It has been stew since Tuesday. It will be stew until we reach the sea.
There is more in it now than there was. I do not ask.

people.name: Herd Girl
lines: This fold holds sixty. We had sixty. I shut the gate myself.
There are fifty-nine, and one in Millbrook. I do not understand how he does it.

people.name: Mrs Alder
lines: Three weeks I have taken these waters, for my nerves.
They taste of egg. I am very nervous about it.

people.name: Attendant
lines: Three cups before breakfast, three after, and a brisk walk to the bench.
It has never cured anybody, but they do sit very nicely.

people.name: Colonel
lines: Bad leg. Other one is worse. Took the waters at Pewter in my day.
East of here is the quarry, and the caves. Do not. Well. I did. Look at my leg.

people.name: Trail Boy
lines: I carry water down to Millbrook for people who cannot come up.
It is mostly just water from the pump, by the time I get there. Do not tell them.

people.name: Old Hob
lines: A boulder came down in my grandad’s day and the fold was shut and everybody forgot.
I did not forget. I just live here now. It is very quiet. Thank you for moving it.

people.name: Clerk’s Mother
lines: Forty years of ledgers in this house and not a penny in any of them.
He does lovely handwriting.

people.name: Shepherd’s Wife
lines: He went up after a lost one on a night raid once, along the track to the old chapel.
He came back. He does not go up at night now. He does not say why. Nor does the dog.

people.name: Rock Picker
lines: It is all the same rock. People pay for it anyway. I do not tell them.
Further up it is the same rock again, and colder.

people.name: Climber
lines: The river is born in this tarn. Follow it down and you come to The Crossing.

people.name: Ganger
lines: Thirty years we have been widening this cutting. It is getting narrower.
Nobody can tell me why. I have stopped asking the rock.

people.name: Navvy
lines: Dig, carry, tip. Dig, carry, tip. The Machop does the carrying.
I have asked what I am for. They said digging. The Machop digs too.

people.name: Pony Girl
lines: They come up here for the summer. I come up here because they will not come down.
Shut the gate when you go. That one knows how to open it, but it likes to be asked.

people.name: Mountain Ranger
lines: Lost on the hill? The Goat Track leaves through the pasture, west of the gorge.
Everybody who comes down that pass is sure they know the way. I have a very good chair.

people.name: Old Wren
lines: Nobody signs the trails in Pine Hollow. You find them or you do not.
The deer go south out of the hollow, down to the broadleaf wood.

people.name: Carter
lines: Everything Millbrook sells comes over that bridge, and I have carried all of it.
My back would like a word with the people who built a village on the wrong side of a river.

people.name: Ostler
lines: That Ponyta bites. No, it does not. It burns. I do not know why I said bites.

people.name: Withy Cutter
lines: Baskets, hurdles, the odd eel trap. It all comes out of this bed.
Your lane there runs down to the stones. Keep your feet.

people.name: Mason
lines: It was going to be the Mayor of Millbrook. Then he stopped paying.
Now it is nobody in particular. It is coming on very well.

people.name: Stone Carter
lines: Up the road for stone, down the road for stone. Up, down.
Some of those are stones. Some of those are Geodude. They are paid the same.

people.name: Angler
lines: Biggest thing in this river is the one my brother did not catch.
I did not catch one nearly as big. Press at the water with a rod, if you have one.

people.name: Brother
lines: He told you about the fish. There was a fish. It was this big.
I show him this big, every year. He has never once believed it.

people.name: Toll Keeper
lines: The bridge is free. It has been free for ninety years. I keep it free.
Somebody has to. You would be surprised how much it costs.

people.name: Stall Girl
lines: Everything here came over that bridge one way, and it is going back the other.
It is cheaper on the way back. Nobody knows why. Do not tell them.

people.name: Stallholder
lines: Honey from the bees, stone from the peaks, eels from the marsh. And me.
I am the only thing here that came from nowhere.

people.name: Lad
lines: East is Tanglewood. Everybody who goes in says it is easy.
Then you see them a day later coming out the other side, very quiet.

people.name: Pip’s Aunt
lines: My nephew in Millbrook says he always wins.
I raced him at Christmas. He started very close.

people.name: Old Drover
lines: Sixty head from the moor to the sea and I lost but the one.
He is in Millbrook. He has a pound of his own now. He has done very well.

people.name: Peddler
lines: East is Tanglewood. I go round it, myself.
Folk who leave that road come out a day later.

people.name: Beekeeper
lines: You tell them everything, bees. Who has married, who has died. They like to know.
I told them about you. They were not interested. Mind the big one.

people.name: Heron Man
lines: A heron can stand still for six hours. I have timed it.
I timed it from here. It took six hours.

people.name: Weir Keeper
lines: The eels come down in autumn, all at once, in the dark, off to the sea.
Nobody has ever seen them come back. They come back, though. Nobody knows how. Eels.

people.name: Burner
lines: You keep it covered and you keep it slow. Six days and you do not sleep.
Then you have got charcoal, and nobody thanks you. Mind the Vulpix. It likes to help.

people.name: Burner’s Wife
lines: Everything I own smells of smoke. That is why I married him. It was the smell or nothing.

people.name: Innkeeper
lines: The coach went into the river in my grandfather’s day. The Ponyta swam out.
We have kept the name. We have kept the Ponyta. It has a room.

people.name: Traveller
lines: Six of us came over the bridge. Five of us are staying for dinner.
I did not ask.

people.name: Pedlar’s Wife
lines: He is out there telling people he goes round Tanglewood.
He got lost in it in the spring. He was gone a week. Do not tell him I told you.

people.name: Keeper’s Wife
lines: He has not taken a penny on that bridge in thirty years, and he is out there every day.
I married a very honest man. I would not recommend it.

people.name: Watcher
lines: There is a slot in the wall for looking at the herons through, and they know about it.
They stand just out of the slot. I have started to take it personally.

people.name: Woodman
lines: We only cut the edge. Nobody who went in to cut the middle has sent any wood back.
Keep to the road. I know everybody says it. Keep to it anyway.

people.name: Young Woodman
lines: There was a deer path here somewhere, just off the road. It comes out at a gap.
If you ever need to leave in a hurry. Which you will. People do.

people.name: Picnic Mum
lines: We said we would just go in as far as the pond.
This is as far as the pond. Nobody is to go any further. Tim. TIM.

people.name: Tim
lines: There is a lane behind that tree that goes all the way to a statue. I saw it.
I saw it from a very long way away. I am not allowed.

people.name: Mushroom Woman
lines: Every lane in this wood is the same lane. I have been picking along it for sixty years.
I go in by the road and I come out by the road. In between I stop thinking about it.
calls: Not that one. Not that one.

people.name: Lost Picnicker
lines: I took one turn off the road for a picnic spot.
That was this morning.

people.name: Woodcutter
lines: Lost? Every path in Tanglewood comes back to the road in the end.
The road is north of here. It always is.

people.name: Quarryman
lines: We broke into this from the quarry above.
Every ladder in here goes down. To cross the vale you go down and come up again.

people.name: Camper Lin
lines: I followed the bats down from the wood.
Now every passage looks like the last one.

people.name: Lost Hiker
lines: This floor is two caves with a wall of rock between.
To get to the other side you go down a floor and back up. I have done it twice.

people.name: Miner
lines: Listen. That rushing is the sea, three floors down.

people.name: Old Miner
lines: We called it the Sleeper.
An Onix, in the east sand. It was lying there before the quarry was dug.

people.name: Fisherman
lines: The tide comes up the passage from the strand.
The Shellder ride in on it and stay.

people.name: Thatcher
lines: Half of Millbrook sleeps under this marsh. It keeps the rain off, mostly.
If you are in a hurry, do not wade. It only feels quicker.

people.name: Reed Boy
lines: I carry the bundles up to the yard. Then they give me more bundles.
That is the whole job. I thought there would be more to it.

people.name: Wildfowler
lines: Sit very still on this bank and the whole marsh comes to you.
Then a raider wades through and it all goes home again.

people.name: Old Bittern
lines: Sixty years I have come out here and I have shot nothing.
I do not own a gun. I just like the hat.

people.name: Mere Fisher
lines: Still as a plate, this mere. I have fished it forty years.
Nothing yet.

people.name: Pond Boy
lines: This pond is not on the map. I checked. So it is mine.
You can look. Looking is free. Fishing is one Poké Ball. Nobody has paid yet.

people.name: Lock Keeper
lines: I open the sluice when the water comes up and shut it when it goes down.
Nobody has told me what happens if I stop. I am not going to be the one who finds out.

people.name: Reed Cutter
lines: We cut the reeds for thatch.
Wade through them if you like. The boardwalk is longer, but you stay dry.

people.name: Tadpole Nan
lines: There are eleven frogs. I have named them all Gerald.
The big one is Big Gerald. He will fight you. He fights everybody.

people.name: Old Seth
lines: My father ran this pump, and his father. It has not pumped anything since the rain.
I still oil it. You do not stop oiling a thing just because it has stopped.
calls: She will go again one day.

people.name: Puntman
lines: Punt goes out to Duck Island and comes back. Walk to the end of the boards and press on.
No, there is nothing out there. Nothing you can eat. There is a hermit. He is not for eating either.

people.name: Eel Wife
lines: Eels go up the drain at night. You can hear them, if you have nothing else to do.
I have nothing else to do.

people.name: Hermit Moss
lines: I came out here to be alone with my thoughts.
There were not as many as I had hoped.
Something is dug in under my good tree. It came with the island. I never looked.

people.name: Eel Seller
lines: Smoked is the good one. Jellied is the one I have got most of.
If you have a rod, the bay is full of them. Please do not. It is my living.

people.name: Mrs Pike
lines: Last winter the bay came up through my floor and took the good chair.
We got it back. It was in the Drowned Duck. They said it floated in.

people.name: Wren
lines: I can swim to the island. Mum says I cannot. I can, though. I just have not.

people.name: Netmaker
lines: Every net in the vale came out of that loft, and every hole in them came out of the Krabby.
Down the coast they pay double. Down the coast they have Krabby.

people.name: Smoker
lines: You smell of smoke now. You will always smell of smoke now.
It is a good smell. You will not get a table anywhere, mind.

people.name: Turf Cutter
lines: Peat is just a marsh that gave up. Cut it, dry it, burn it.
It takes a thousand years to grow a spade of it. I do about four hundred a day.

people.name: Turf Boy
lines: Dad says those Diglett do more than I do.
They do. They are very good. They do not take a wage. I have spoken to them about it.

people.name: Birder Tess
lines: Hush. The ducks only come in when nobody wades the reeds.
One of those has not moved in a week. I am beginning to think it is a Lapras doll.

people.name: Mrs Osier
lines: Baskets for the eels, baskets for the peat, baskets to put the other baskets in.
My sister at The Crossing says hers are better. They are not. Do not tell her I said so.

people.name: Old Reeve
lines: I collected the toll on the Mere Path for thirty years. There is no toll now.
I still sit here. Somebody ought to.
West, and do not stop for anybody on the path. Nobody good is out there.

people.name: Snipe Shooter
lines: You have walked all this way into the reeds to talk to me. I do not know what to do with that.
Nobody comes up here. That is what it is for.

people.name: Birdwatcher
lines: Birdwatching. That is what I am doing. With these crates. Which are for birds.
Cove? What cove? There is no cove down that path. Very rocky, the no cove.

people.name: Landlady
lines: Beds are full. Beds are always full. There are two of them.
The duck is not for looking at. It is stuffed. It is a very sad story and it costs extra.

people.name: Old Soak
lines: There is a hermit on that island owes me eleven years of ale.
Tell him I said hello. Tell him I said eleven.

people.name: Eel Man
lines: Same seat, same pint, forty years. I have asked them to move the door, it lets the bay in.
They have asked me to move.

people.name: Young Pike
lines: Mum says we have to keep the door shut or the bay gets in.
It got in anyway. Look at the floor.

people.name: Net Mender
lines: Every hole in every net in the vale comes through this room.
You would not believe the holes. I have seen a hole that was mostly hole.

people.name: Old Ness
lines: The boats go out from the end of the jetty.
There is a cave under the cliffs. The tide hides it.

people.name: Beachcomber
lines: Everything the sea takes off the wreck ends up in this cove.
Mind the Krabby. They think it is theirs.

people.name: Fisherman
lines: The Magikarp come up from the sea this far, and no further.

people.name: Kite Flyer
lines: The wind off the sea takes my kite right over the cliffs!
That is four kites. There is a very well-off Krabby down there.

people.name: Old Bertie
lines: Lit her every night for forty years, and nobody has told me to stop.
They did tell me. I did not catch it. My hearing is very selective.

people.name: Ropemaker
lines: Forty fathoms a day, walking backwards. I have not seen where I was going since I was twelve.
If that Mankey has the end of it again, I am not going to know until the far post.
calls: Mind your back. Mine, I mean.

people.name: Rope Boy
lines: I turn the wheel. He walks away. Then I turn the wheel some more. He is nearly at Pewter.

people.name: Sexton
lines: There is nobody under most of these. The sea keeps them. These are just where to come and shout.
I have got a good one for you, down in the far corner. He is not dead. He owes me for the stone.

people.name: Salt Raker
lines: Sea goes in, sun comes out, sea goes away, you rake what is left.
Everything tastes of it. My wife tastes of it. It is a very nice marriage.

people.name: Net Wife
lines: Every boat out of this strand has got one of my nets on it, and every net has got a hole.
They say I do not mend them. I say they keep finding Krabby.

people.name: Drying Rack Dan
lines: Salt, wind and three days on the rack. Then you could mend a boot with it.
People have. Those boots are very well thought of.

people.name: Fishwife
lines: Fresh in this morning. Which morning, I could not swear to.
If it looks back at you, that is how you know.

people.name: Fisher Lad
lines: I went on the boat once. Out to the end of the jetty.
They say past that there are islands. They say there is ice on one, and on the other a mountain on fire.
I think they say that to get you on the boat.

people.name: Stage Angler
lines: Good bit of stage, this. Tide comes up through the boards at the spring.
Press at the water with a rod, if you have one. There is a Tentacool I am not speaking to.

people.name: Gorse Burner
lines: Burn it back every spring or the whole heath goes to gorse.
It goes to gorse anyway. It is very good at it. I am quite fond of it.

people.name: Salt Carter
lines: Salt to the boats, fish to the salt, boats to the fish. I have been up and down this hill all my life.
I got to The Crossing once. It was all right.

people.name: Wracker
lines: Three crates this week, and one of them full of dolls. What is it with that ship and dolls?
Something is under the sand by that log. I keep meaning to dig, but it might be somebody’s.

people.name: Wracker’s Girl
lines: I found a boot. Then I found another boot. They are not the same boot.
I am going to keep looking until I find somebody with one of each.

people.name: Courting Couple
lines: You can see the whole coast from up here. Yes. That is why we come. The coast.

people.name: Bertie’s Niece
lines: We have told him. We have told him in writing. He uses it to light the lamp.

people.name: Old Skipper
lines: Forty years I fished off that strand and I have never yet seen the Mere Punt come out to sea.
It is a very small boat. They are very sensible.

people.name: Mrs Sprat
lines: The lower town was my mother’s. You can see her roof, at low water, off the end of the jetty.
We did not sell it. It sort of went.

people.name: Farmer Hale
lines: Hop the terraces if you are in a hurry. Mind, you will not climb back.

people.name: Picker
lines: These are the old trees. The best apples are always the highest ones.

people.name: Shell Digger
lines: The tide leaves the best shells right at the far end of the sands!

people.name: Old Ohm
lines: The turbines stopped the year the Card Key went missing.
Last I heard it was dropped in the pines, out west.

people.name: Linesman
lines: The turbines have not turned since the flood.
The falls still try. Listen to them.

people.name: Night Watchman
lines: There is a steel shutter on the floor below.
Only the Card Key opens it, and the card was lost in the pines.

people.name: Guard
lines: The shutter takes the Card Key. The lift takes power.
Nobody gets down here by accident.

people.name: Grunt
lines: Step on an arrow and the floor carries you till something stops you.
The generator is across all that. Took me a week.

people.name: Scientist
lines: The lift only runs once the generator on the floor above is back on.
Whoever did that, thank you. I was down here a long time.

people.name: Warden
lines: Welcome to the reserve.
Pokemon live in these reeds that you will not find anywhere else in the vale.

people.name: Beachcomber
lines: The bar to the wreck only shows at low water.
Whatever the sea throws up on it is anybody's.

people.name: Salvager's Wife
lines: Ned has been out on that wreck since the tide turned.
If you see him, tell him his tea is cold.

people.name: Flood Warden
lines: The sea came over the wall and never went home.
The sandbags hold the lower streets. Most days.

people.name: Harbourmaster
lines: The sea took the lower town in one winter.
At low water you can walk the old streets to the stair.

people.name: Old Rook
lines: The boat goes out when the tide turns, and not before.
You never saw this cove. Nobody ever has.

people.name: Climber
lines: I came up for the view and the storm came with me.
Something small and pink watches from the cairn.

people.name: Cragsman
lines: The shelves go round the crags, one above the other.
The cairn is on the top. Mind the lightning.

people.name: Spelunker
lines: I am mapping the deepest floor.
Up the far passage there is daylight, and a storm.

people.name: Gravedigger
lines: You only find this place at night, by the sheep track.
The Gastly do no harm. Mostly.

people.name: Channeler
lines: I am a CHANNELER.
There are spirits up to mischief.
I sense them under the floor.

people.name: Mourner
lines: I came to pray for my dearly departed CLEFAIRY.
Sniff!

people.name: Old Whaler
lines: The lagoon is the other side of the berg. The cave under it is ice the whole way.
Once you are moving on ice you go till something stops you. Look before you step.
Our boat comes into the lagoon late, for anyone who got that far.

people.name: Ice Fisher
lines: The hole down is in the far corner, past the ice.
Stop against the right boulder and you are there. Stop against the wrong one and you go round again.

people.name: Lookout
lines: The skiff runs back to the cove till our boat sails. Half past two, and not a minute after.
Miss it and you are here till the burners go.

people.name: Charcoal Burner
lines: Our boat takes the charcoal off at twenty past three. There is room for one more.
The crater is ash all the way down, and something lives in every step of it.

people.name: Volcanologist
lines: The mountain breathes. Feel the ground? Warm.
It has not gone up in a hundred years. I am waiting.

people.name: Burners' Lad
lines: The tube runs on under the crater. Hot underfoot all the way.
MILLBROOK
Where every road in the vale starts.
MILL SQUARE
West: the Westward Road. North: the moor. East: The Crossing. South: Reedmere.
South to REEDMERE
Down the lane, past the pool and the woodcutter.
North to HIGH MOOR
Up the drove road, past the Grey Stones.
NOTICES
LOST: one coin purse, at the mill, on Tuesday. Reward. Ask nobody. They will only look for it.
FOR SALE: pond. Slightly used.
WANTED: somebody with a Cut to do Hazel’s hedge. It has been years.
MILL LANE
The mill is open. The miller is not, before noon.
THE ALLOTMENTS
Please do not eat the seedlings. This means you, Oddish.
THE ORCHARD
Pick what you like. Take what you can carry. The berries grow back.
HIGH MOOR
The drove road climbs to Moor Top, then north over the moor.
East: GREYSTONE PEAKS
North: the Grey Stones and the Moor Gate.
THE MOOR GATE
The old toll road leaves the vale here.
THE LITTLE STONES
There are nine. There were seven. Do not ask. Please put back any you borrow.
MOOR SPRING
The waters cure gout, grief and the common cold. Results may vary. They have varied.
THE SHEPHERD’S
Mind the flock. Nothing here is a sheep. We do not discuss it.
THE DROVERS’ FOLD
Shut the gate. Count the herd. Count them again. Accept the second number.
THE LOST FOLD
Nobody has brought a beast up here since the boulder came down. Everyone has meant to.
THE GREY STONES
The tor the vale is named for. The drovers touch it for luck.
THE WAYSTONES
They walked down from the tor one night. So the drovers say. Do not count them.
GREYSTONE PEAKS
The pass climbs through the cutting and round the head of the tarn.
THE TARN
The river starts here, under the summit.
THE HIGH PASTURE
Shut the gate behind you. The ponies wander.
THE PASS
Down: The Crossing. Up: the caves, the quarry and the tarn.
THE CUTTING
Driven through by hand. Do not ask whose. Falling rock: yes.
RANGER POST
Lost? Stay where you are. Somebody will be along. That somebody is also lost.
THE CROSSING
Over the bridge: Bridge End. Tanglewood east, the peaks north, the strand south.
North: GREYSTONE PEAKS
East: TANGLEWOOD. South: GULL STRAND.
THE CROSSING
West: Millbrook and the Mill Square.
THE WEST BANK
Bridge ahead. Carters give way to nobody. Do not stand behind the Ponyta.
The road south
Down to Gull Strand and the sea.
THE COACH AND PONYTA
Hot food. Warm beds. Do not ask about the coach.
THE STONE YARD
Grey Stone cut to order. Statues by arrangement. Please do not sit on the statue. It is not finished.
THE ANGLERS’ STAGE
Members only. Membership is free. Fish are extra.
THE BEE GARDEN
Nothing here will sting you if you are polite. Be polite.
HERON WALK
Please keep to the boards. The herons will not. They have been told.
Nothing signposted
If you can read this you have gone wrong, or right. The burners do not mind.
TANGLEWOOD
East to the Eastern Track. Keep to the road.
WOODMEN’S STAND
Wood for The Crossing and the vale. Mind the logs. The logs do not mind you.
THE PICNIC GROUND
As far as the pond. No further. We mean it. We have told you now.
Chalked on the rock:
DOWN - THE WOOD, ONE FLOOR. DOWN - THE SEA, FOUR FLOORS.
Scratched on the rock by the hole:
COLD WIND FROM BELOW. NOBODY CAME BACK UP THIS WAY.
REEDMERE
The boardwalk goes round. The reeds go through.
THE HUMMOCK
The only dry ground for a mile. Please leave some of it for the next person.
PRIVATE POND
Not on any map. Keep out. This means you. Signed, the Owner (age nine).
THE LONG DRAIN
Dug by hand in the old days, by people who had been told it would help.
THE OLD PUMP
It drained this whole fen once. Then it rained.
THE MERE PUNT
Out to Duck Island and back. No charge. Mind the ducks. They do not mind you.
EELS
Smoked, jellied, or looked at. Ask at the stall.
MERE END
East: the staithe, the old pump and Gull Strand. West: the duck hide and the Mere Path.
THE DROWNED DUCK
Beds. Ale. No, you may not see the duck.
THE DUCK HIDE
QUIET PLEASE. The ones on the bank are real. The one in the water is a doll. Tess knows.
THE WITHY BEDS
Cut every seven years. Do not lean on them.
THE MERE PATH
West, out of the marsh. Last dry bed for a long way. Ask at the house.
NOTHING DOWN THIS PATH
Nothing at all. Certainly not a cove. Go back.
THE TURBARY
Peat for the whole marsh. Cut it, stack it, turn it, swear at it.
GULL STRAND
East: the orchards. South: the strand and the jetty.
GULL STRAND
West: Reedmere. East: the stone bridge. The cliff path goes down to the cove.
THE OLD LIGHT
Not lit since the boats got radios. Trimmed daily. Nobody has told Bertie.
THE ROPE WALK
Walk backwards. Keep walking. That is the whole of the trade.
THE SAILORS’ REST
They went out from the jetty. Some of them came back as far as this.
THE SALT PANS
Keep off the pans. Wade if you must. Do not lick anything.
THE QUAY
Fish off the boats by noon. After noon, ask the cat.
WRACKERS’ SAND
What the sea leaves is yours. What the sea wants back, it takes. Check the tide.
THE SANDS
Along the sands west, the cockle path goes up through the wood.
ORCHARD TERRACES
The lane is east. The terraces are down, and the ledges are quicker.
THE LANE
East: The Wreck, on the cape. West and up: the farm.
Scratched on the wall:
THE BOULDERS UPSTAIRS MOVE. IT TAKES SOMETHING STRONG.
GREYSTONE POWER STATION
Service gate locked. Card Key holders only.
PYLON ROAD
North: along the reservoir and out of the vale.
SAFARI ZONE
South: the marsh reserve.
STAFF ONLY
Plant room below. Keep the shutter locked.
ELEVATOR
Runs off the B2F generator. If it stops, switch it back on.
SAFARI MARSH
A warden's reserve. Keep to the paths; the reeds are full.
THE WRECK
The liner went onto the reef in the last storm. The camp is below the cliff.
THE CAPE
The wreck is out on the reef, past the camp. The pier is east.
THE ICE RUN
The launch runs out to Frostreef on the flood tide.
It sails from 2:00 until 4:00.
THE SUNKEN QUARTER
The old high street. Mind the tide.
STORMCROWN
The path climbs round the three crags to the cairn.
THE CLOUD STAIR
Over the top, and down the far side out of the storm.
Scratched deep in the rock:
NO WAY BACK BUT UP.
DROVERS' BOTHY
The drovers slept here the night before the fair.
LANTERN CROSS
Lit for the drovers coming over the fell after dark.
THE MOOR CHAPEL
Erected in the memory of the drovers and their POKéMON.
THE CORPSE ROAD
West, off the fell.
STATION MASTER'S GARDEN
Please keep to the paths.
FROSTREEF
The launch puts in on the flood tide. When the tide turns, it does not.
EMBER ISLE
The path climbs the south face to the Lava Tube. The crater is past it.
LAVA TUBE
The only way into the crater. Mind your step on the ash.
THE BLACK SANDS
The island makes its own beach. The boat is at the jetty on the west shore.

trainers.name: Scout Tam
lines: You look like you have got a minute. You have not. Battle me anyway!

trainers.name: Orchardist Bea
lines: Those are my apples, and that is my good ladder.

trainers.name: Drover Hale
lines: This road is for the herd!
Show me your Pokemon if you want to pass.

trainers.name: Breaker Finn
lines: This quarry is closed to visitors!
Unless you can break through me.

trainers.name: Collier Bram
lines: I burn charcoal under the old oak. Nobody comes this far in.

trainers.name: Netter Bryn
lines: The bridge is my spot!
Let us see what you have caught.

trainers.name: Breaker Dunn
lines: I break rocks all day. Put your Pokemon down there and let us see.

trainers.name: Collier Osk
lines: Six days I have sat up with this stack. I could do with the company!

trainers.name: Bug Catcher Tam
lines: Everyone gets lost in here. That is how I catch them.

trainers.name: Hiker Gorse
lines: Mind the sand. It sinks under you.

trainers.name: Collier Wyn
lines: There was coal down here once. Now there is only me.

trainers.name: Collier Dunn
lines: Do not wake the Sleeper. I have to work next to it.

trainers.name: Smuggler Gill
lines: That rope is spoken for.

trainers.name: Netter Fen
lines: The mere is mine at this hour. Fight for it!

trainers.name: Fowler Hugh
lines: You have put up every bird on the marsh. You can pay for them.

trainers.name: Bog Walker Rue
lines: I walk the bog for my health. It is terrible for my health. Battle me!

trainers.name: Raider Kit
lines: The strand is mine at low tide. Fight!

trainers.name: Orchardist Pip
lines: Paws off my apples!

trainers.name: Damkeeper Volt
lines: Nobody touches the sluices but me!

trainers.name: Grunt
lines: Who let you down here? The shutter was locked!

trainers.name: Grunt
lines: You came through the arrows? Then you can go back the same way!

trainers.name: Grunt
lines: The war room is off limits. Orders are orders!

trainers.name: Ranger Moss
lines: The ranger's track is mine to keep. Show me what you caught!

trainers.name: Salvager Ned
lines: This camp has first pick of the wreck!
You want a share, you earn it.

trainers.name: Diver Coral
lines: I dive the mansion cellars. Finders keepers!

trainers.name: Grunt
lines: Hey! That cargo is spoken for!

trainers.name: Hiker Brann
lines: Nobody climbs Stormcrown without a fight!

trainers.name: Hiker Rudd
lines: Nobody comes this deep for the view.

trainers.name: Gardener Rowan
lines: These beds were the station master's pride. Mind where you tread!

trainers.name: Smuggler
lines: Nobody comes through the tube but us!

trainers.name: Smuggler
lines: That hoard is the whole run. Hands off it!
